t: The President shall include with each budget for a fiscal year submitted to the Congress under section 1105 of title 31, United States Code, materials that shall identify clearly and separately the amounts requested in the budget for appropriation for that fiscal year for salaries and expenses related to administrative activities of the Department of Defense, the military departments, and the defense agencies.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a formal submission requirement is participatory, but this only requires the President to include budget materials for Congress identifying Department of Defense administrative costs. Both the President and Congress are inside the federal government, so nothing crosses the federal boundary. There is no public comment, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: The President shall include with each budget for a fiscal year submitted to the Congress

qwen_block.w: This section requires the President to submit specific budgetary information to Congress. Both the President and Congress are part of the federal government. The definition explicitly states that reports to or notifications of Congress are inside the federal government and do not constitute participation. There is no involvement of outside parties such as the public, states, or private entities in this decision-making process.
qwen_block.s: The President shall include with each budget for a fiscal year submitted to the Congress under section 1105 of title 31, United States Code, materials that shall identify clearly and separately the amounts requested in the budget for appropriation for that fiscal year for salaries and expenses related to administrative activities of the Department of Defense, the military departments, and the defense agencies.

opus.w: This section only requires the President to give Congress budget materials. Both the President and Congress are inside the federal government. Someone might read a formal submission to Congress as participation, but it is reporting within the government. No state, expert, company or member of the public is consulted, and there is no comment period, hearing, advisory body or right to sue.
opus.s: The President shall include with each budget for a fiscal year submitted to the Congress under section 1105 of title 31, United States Code, materials that shall identify clearly and separately the amounts requested

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the President to submit budget materials to Congress. According to the definition, Congress is inside the federal government, so reporting to it is not participation with an outside party. There is no mention of consulting with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities.
qwen_chat.s: The President shall include with each budget for a fiscal year submitted to the Congress under section 1105 of title 31, United States Code, materials that shall identify clearly and separately the amounts requested in the budget for appropriation for that fiscal year for salaries and expenses related to administrative activities of the Department of Defense, the military departments, and the defense agencies.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the budget is submitted to Congress, and Congress is a separate branch of government, this constitutes "participation" or consultation with an outside entity. However, the definition explicitly states that "Congress, its committees and members... are all INSIDE the federal government." Therefore, reporting to Congress is intra-governmental communication, not participation with an outside party. Furthermore, the section describes a unilateral reporting requirement by the President, not a process of consulting with or coordinating with external stakeholders (like states, tribes, or the public) before making a decision.
